title: Australian Student Visa 2025: New Rules & Requirements
excerpt: Learn the 2025 Australian student visa rules, fees, work limits, requirements, and tips to apply successfully as an international student in Australia.
html:
If you’re planning to study in Australia in 2025, it’s crucial to understand the latest Australian student visa requirements, updated fees, and new policy changes. Australia remains one of the most popular destinations for international students, offering world-class universities, vibrant cities, and a pathway to valuable work experience.

However, the Australian government has introduced stricter financial proof, higher English proficiency standards, and tighter scrutiny under the Genuine Student requirement, all aimed at ensuring only genuine applicants are approved. These changes affect everything, from how much you must show in savings to how many hours you can work during term time.

Whether you’re applying for the first time or renewing your visa, this comprehensive guide will help you stay informed, avoid common mistakes, and prepare a strong application that meets all updated criteria.

What Is the Australian Student Visa?

The Australian student visa (subclass 500) allows international students to live, study, and gain work experience in Australia legally.

With this visa, you can:

  • Enroll in full-time courses at government-registered institutions (CRICOS providers)
  • Bring eligible family members, such as your partner or children, as dependents
  • Work limited hours (currently 48 hours per fortnight) while studying to help cover living expenses
  • Stay in Australia for the duration of your course plus additional time for graduation or travel
  • Apply for a Post-Study Work Visa (subclass 485) after completing your studies if you meet the eligibility criteria

This visa is the main pathway for international students to access Australia’s high-quality education system and explore future work and migration opportunities.

New Australian Student Visa Rules in 2025

Here are the major updates announced by the Department of Home Affairs:

Increased Financial Requirements

From 2025, students must show higher savings evidence to cover living costs:

  • AUD $29,710/year for living expenses (up from AUD $24,505)
  • Additional funds if bringing dependents

Tip: Keep updated as these amounts are revised annually.

Higher English Language Requirements

New minimum English test scores are required:

  • IELTS: Overall 6.0 (no band below 5.5)
  • TOEFL iBT: Minimum 64
  • PTE Academic: Minimum 50
  • Cambridge: 169

This change aims to ensure students are ready for academic study and work.

Work Hour Rules

From July 2023, and continuing in 2025:

  • 48 hours per fortnight (24 hrs/week) during study periods
  • Unlimited hours during semester breaks

This replaces the temporary unlimited work rights introduced during COVID-19.

If you want a detailed guide about work hour rules, you can refer to Student Visa Working Hours in Australia 2025.

Streamlined Genuine Student (GS) Requirement

The previous Genuine Temporary Entrant (GTE) requirement is being replaced by a Genuine Student (GS) test, focusing on:

  • Academic background and progression
  • Language capability
  • Financial capacity
  • Post-study intentions

This change tightens scrutiny of applications.

Health Insurance & Medical Exams

All students must maintain Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) throughout their stay.

Medical Tests May Include:

  • Chest X-ray
  • HIV, Hepatitis screening
  • General health exam

Requirements vary by country of origin and length of stay.

Australian Student Visa Fees in 2025

Here’s the updated fee structure:

Applicant TypeVisa Fee (AUD)
Main applicant$710
Dependent over 18$530
Dependent under 18$175

Fees are subject to change, therefore confirm on the Department of Home Affairs site before applying.

Australian Student Visa Requirements

To apply, you’ll need:

  • Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE)
  • Valid passport
  • OSHC policy
  • Financial evidence covering tuition, living costs, travel
  • English test results
  • SOP letter (statement of purpose)
  • Completed Form 157A
  • Biometrics and medical checks as requested

SOP Letter for Australian Student Visa

The Statement of Purpose (SOP) is critical. It should:

  • Explain why you chose Australia
  • Detail your course and institution
  • Outline your academic and professional goals
  • Demonstrate intent to comply with visa conditions

Tip: Be genuine and clear, generic or templated SOPs can lead to refusals.

Australian Student Visa Processing Time

Most applications are processed within 4–6 weeks, depending on:

  • Your country of residence
  • Course type
  • Completeness of documents
  • Health and character checks
  • Apply early to avoid delays.

Benefits of Studying in Australia

  • Access to world-class universities
  • Work while studying to offset costs
  • Pathways to post-study work visas and PR
  • Multicultural environment

Also read our latest blog on Affordable Public Colleges in Canada for Students in 2025.

FAQs

1: What is the new minimum financial requirement?

As of 2025, you must show at least AUD $29,710/year for living expenses.

2: Can I work full-time during my studies?

No, work is limited to 48 hours per fortnight while classes are in session.

3: Is medical insurance mandatory?

Yes, you must have an Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC).

4: Has the GTE requirement changed?

Yes, it’s now called the Genuine Student (GS) requirement with stricter checks.

5: Can I stay in Australia after graduating?

Yes, graduates may be eligible for a Post-Study Work Visa (subclass 485).

Final Thoughts

Australia remains one of the best destinations for international education, but the 2025 updates mean higher standards, stricter financial proof, and more rigorous checks on student intentions. These changes are designed to protect the integrity of the visa system and ensure that only genuine students are approved.

Stay informed, prepare strong documentation, and consider professional advice to improve your success chances. With careful planning and the right guidance, you can confidently start your study journey and make the most of everything Australia has to offer.

Choosing the right college is one of the biggest decisions you’ll make when planning to study abroad. This guide explains why public colleges in Canada are such a popular option, how they differ from universities, and what you should know about tuition, admissions, and work opportunities.

Why Study at a Public College in Canada?

Public colleges in Canada are funded by provincial governments, which helps keep tuition more affordable while ensuring consistent quality standards.

Here’s why thousands of international students choose them every year:

  • Lower Tuition Fees: Compared to universities, public colleges cost less per year.
  • Shorter Programs: Diplomas and certificates often take 1–2 years.
  • Hands-on Learning: Programs emphasize real-world skills and practical training.
  • PGWP Eligibility: Graduates can often apply for the Post-Graduate Work Permit to gain Canadian work experience.
  • Diverse Student Community: Colleges enroll students from over 150 countries.

Tip: Public colleges are ideal if your goal is career-focused training and a faster path to employment.

Why These Colleges Rank Among the Best in Canada

  • Canadian colleges are highly regarded due to their.
  • Strong industry connections that ensure curriculum relevance and enhance graduate employability.
  • Affordable tuition fees, making quality education accessible to international students.

  • Comprehensive student support services encompassing housing, academics, and career development.

DLI Number

Program Strength

Research and choose a recognized public college that offers your desired program and fits your goals.

Yes. Diplomas from recognized Canadian public colleges are accepted as valid educational credentials for various immigration pathways, including Express Entry (Federal Skilled Worker Program), Provincial Nominee Programs (PNPs), and Canadian Experience Class (CEC), especially when combined with relevant Canadian work experience obtained through the Post-Graduate Work Permit (PGWP)

10: What medical insurance is required for Nepali students in Canadian colleges?

International students in Canada, including those from Nepal, are required to have provincial health insurance in provinces with public health plans covering international students (like British Columbia, Ontario) or must purchase private health insurance where public plans are unavailable (e.g., Quebec). Colleges typically provide guidance on the mandatory health coverage and its costs during admission

11:How does the cost of studying in a Canadian public college compare to Australia or the UK?

Canadian public colleges generally offer more affordable tuition fees and lower living costs compared to similar colleges in Australia and the UK. Annual tuition fees for international students at Canadian public colleges range roughly from CAD 15,000 to CAD 22,000, while living expenses vary by city but are often lower than major Australian or UK student cities.

12: What are the most common reasons for student visa refusal from Nepal?

Common reasons for Canada student visa refusals from Nepal include:

  • Insufficient proof of funds or financial backing
  • Incomplete or incorrect documentation
  • Lack of convincing ties to Nepal indicating intention to return
  • Poor presentation of study plan or purpose of study
  • Previous immigration violations or rejections

Final Thoughts

Public colleges in Canada provide excellent value, hands-on learning, and a gateway to a Canadian career. With over 100 publicly funded institutions across the country, you have a wide range of choices to match your budget and goals.

Explore your options, compare programs carefully, and start your journey with confidence.

What Is the Post Graduate Work Permit (PGWP)?

The Post Graduate Work Permit Canada allows eligible international students to work in Canada after program completion. Its duration depends on your study program:

  • Programs 2+ years: Eligible for up to 3-year PGWP
  • 8 months to <2 years: PGWP matches program length
  • Multiple programs: Total PGWP equals combined duration, if all completed consecutively

  • Eligible fields include Agriculture, STEM, Transportation, Healthcare, Trades, plus Education (added Dec 2024)
  • Language tests mandatory:
    • University degrees: CLB 7 (English/French)
    • College diplomas: CLB 5 in all four skills

Positive Update (March 2025)

  • College grads in degree programs no longer face field restrictions; only language criteria now apply

You can refer to our blog on Canada Student Visa 2025 for more detailed insights about Canada visa rules and requirements.

Canada PGWP Eligibility Expansion

  • Applies to grads from bachelor’s, master’s, doctoral programs, even in colleges; no field-of-study restrictions
  • Diploma/certificate grads must be in eligible fields
  • Flight school grads exempt from field/language requirements if licensed
  • Program transferers—new study permit may disqualify from PGWP under new rules as of Nov 2024

PGWP Extensions & Passport Tips

  • Your passport must cover the full PGWP duration
  • To extend due to a short-validity passport, apply by paper after passport renewal
  • Extensions must be filed 30 days before expiration

Courses Eligible for PGWP in Canada

  • Flight school programs and higher-degree college programs also remain eligible
  • If you are unsure, please check your CIP code and consult official IRCC resources

PGWP to Permanent Resident (PR) Canada

Post graduate work permit to permanent resident Canada is a key pathway:

  • PGWP gives Canadian work experience, vital for Express Entry
  • Many apply under Canadian Experience Class (CEC) with 1+ year skilled work
  • PGWP + Canadian experience = higher PR chances

PGWP Canada New Rules to Watch

  • Field restrictions no longer apply to degree college grads (Mar 2025)
  • Language criteria apply across all study levels
  • No program switching or study permit extensions after Nov 2024 without losing PGWP eligibility

Up to 3 years, depending on program length and eligibility

  • Medical Exam: Undergo a medical examination if necessary.
  • Intent to Leave: Convince the immigration officer that you’ll leave Canada upon permit expiry.

html:
Considering continuing your education in the United Kingdom? Obtaining a UK student visa is the first and most significant step in the process. Be it a top-tier university or a specialized college, having a clear understanding of UK student visa requirements, charges, and the application process will keep you ready.

In this meticulous guide, you’ll learn about the entire process of applying for a UK student visa which includes, but is not limited to, UK student visa application, including the student visa UK cost, processing time, and eligibility.

What is a UK Student Visa?

The UK student visa, or Tier 4 visa, permits international students to enroll and study with full-time courses in the UK. This visa also allows part-time employment and provides avenues for further work opportunities after graduation through the Graduate Route.

Student Visa UK Requirements (2025)

As with any other visa, application processes for a UK student visa has its own prerequisites which need to be complied with prior to applying. In this case, UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) determines eligibility.

Notable requirements for the student visa UK include:

  • Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) from a licensed sponsor (university or college)
  • Proof of financial ability (tuition fees + living expenses)
  • Valid passport or travel document
  • Proof of English language proficiency (IELTS, PTE, or equivalent)
  • Tuberculosis test results (if applicable)
  • Visa application fee and Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS)

UK Student Visa Fee in 2025

Gathering sufficient funds and traveling within the United Kingdom comes with its expenses, so estimating the total cost of acquiring a UK student visa remains fundamental in managing finances. Also, the cost of the visa and associated payments are not the only expenses to keep in mind.

Breakdown of Student Visa Fee & Related Costs:

Expense TypeEstimated Cost (GBP)Details
Student Visa Application Fee£490Mandatory for all international students.
Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS)£776 per yearCovers NHS healthcare access during your stay.
Priority Visa Service (optional)£500+Decision in 5 working days (optional service).
Super Priority Visa Service£1,000+24-hour processing (for urgent cases).
Biometrics Appointment Fee£75 – £100Depending on your local visa application centre.
Document Scanning/Uploading Services£50 – £100Optional if you need assistance uploading docs.

Important: Always check the latest rates on the UK Government Visa & Immigration website as fees can change based on policy updates.

UK Student Visa Processing Time

The average UK student visa processing time is around 3 weeks. However, keep in mind that this estimate only starts the clock after you submit all biometric data and the required documents at the visa application center.

Some students think that filling out the online form kicks off the clock. The official start of processing time is when biometrics are collected.

Important Considerations:

  • During the high demand periods, for example July through September, processing time may be exceeded due to increased application volumes.
  • Providing documents that are incomplete, blurry scans, or missing proof of funds will result in additional processing which can significantly extend the wait for the visa.
  • Certain countries might take slightly longer processing times based on local UKVI office capacity and workload.

Realistic Expectation:

Although almost all students get a response in under 15 working days, it is best to budget a 4-6 week cushion from application submission to visa approval, especially during peak times.

Pro Tip: Always monitor the progress of your application using the UKVI official tracking system and pay close attention to any prompts for supplementary information.

How to Apply for UK Student Visa: Step-by-Step

Here’s how to apply for student visa UK in 2025:

Step 1: Get Your CAS Letter

Receive the Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies from your university or college.

Step 2: Prepare Your Documents

Collect all documents, including financial proof, passport, CAS, English test results, and medical test if required.

Step 3: Fill Out Online Visa Application

Visit the official UK government website and apply for UK student visa online.

Step 4: Pay Visa Fee & IHS

Use an international payment method to pay the UK student visa fee and immigration surcharge.

Step 5: Book a Visa Appointment

Attend your appointment at the nearest visa application center (VAC) to submit biometrics and documents.

Step 6: Wait for Decision

Track your application status and wait for approval.

Also read our latest blog on How to Get PR in Australia as an International Student.

FAQs

1. How much is the UK student visa fee in 2025?

The student visa fee in UK for international students is set at £490. In addition, you will have to pay £776 annually as a Immigration Health Surcharge.

2. What are the student visa UK requirements?

You must obtain a CAS letter, financial proof, a passport, English language proficiency test score, and a Tuberculosis test in some cases. Every document must comply strictly with UKVI regulations.

3. How long does the UK student visa take to process?

The typical UK student visa processing time is 3 weeks from the date of your visa appointment. There is also an option for expedited processing at an additional cost which takes 5 working days.

4. When should I apply for UK student visa?

As an international applicant, you are allowed to apply for UK student visa up to 6 months prior to the start date of the course.

5. What is the total cost of applying for a UK student visa?

If you are planning to study for one year, expect to spend approximately £1,266 or more which includes visa application and health surcharge fee. This is excluding university application and travel expenses.

Conclusion

Acquiring a UK student visa should not be a difficult task. With proper planning, understanding the student visa UK requirements, and budget management, the process can be streamlined. Always finalize your supporting documents far in advance and check that all info is accurate and complete.

With this guide, you’re one step closer to making your UK education dream a reality.

title: How to Get PR in Australia as an International Student
excerpt: Learn how to get PR in Australia after study. Discover PR courses, visa options, point system, and steps to apply for permanent residency in Australia.
html:
Numerous international students wish to convert their visit into an extended opportunity in Australia. If you are among the individuals, figuring out how to get PR in Australia (Permanent Residency) would be the first step to realize your dreams in this globally acclaimed nation.

By reading this article carefully till the end, you will understand the eligibility criteria for PR in Australia, the PR points system, recommended courses for permanent residency in Australia, and the smoothed process for applying for the PR in Australia.

What is PR in Australia?

A non-citizen is permitted to live, work and study in Australia without any time restrictions through Permanent Residency (PR). PR holders are provided with rights similar to that of an Australian citizen which entails access to health care services, social security, as well as the ability to sponsor family members.

How to Get PR in Australia: Step-by-Step Process

Here’s a simplified overview of the process for international students:

1. Complete a PR-Eligible Course

Select one of the courses that offers a pathway to Australia’s permanent residency. Such courses are often associated with professions that appear on the Skilled Occupation List (SOL).

Some popular PR courses in Australia are:

  • Nursing
  • Information technology
  • Engineering
  • Accounting
  • Social Work
  • Trade courses (plumbing, cookery, automotive and so on)

These courses improve your chances of being employed in highly sought after areas which considerably aids in meeting the Australia PR requirements.

2. Apply for a Temporary Graduate Visa (Subclass 485)

Once you complete your course, apply for the Temporary Graduate Visa which enables you to live and work in Australia for a period of 2 to 4 years.

Such work experience can:

  • Make it easier for you to acquire additional PR points in Australia
  • Increase your employability
  • Improve your PR application

3. Check Your Eligibility and PR Points

The General Skilled Migration (GSM) program is based on a point system. A minimum of 65 points is required for you to be able to apply for direct permanent residency (PR).

Determining Factors For PR Points Include:

  • Age (most points if between 25–32 years old)
  • Mastery of the English Language (IELTS, PTE, etc.)
  • Australian degrees
  • Employment in Australia or abroad
  • Nomination from State or Region
  • Spouse’s qualifications/supporting documents

Calculate your points using an official PR points calculator.

4. Choose the Right PR Visa Pathway

There are several visa subclasses through which you can apply for PR in Australia:

Visa TypeDescription
Skilled Independent Visa (Subclass 189)For skilled workers with no sponsor
Skilled Nominated Visa (Subclass 190)For applicants nominated by a state/territory
Skilled Work Regional Visa (Subclass 491)For those willing to live and work in regional areas
Employer Nomination Scheme (Subclass 186)Requires employer sponsorship
Permanent Partner Visa (Subclass 801)For those with an Australian partner

Depending on the visa, there are specific Australia PR requirements that must be adhered to, select the one that most accurately caters to your circumstances. You can check the services page on our website to learn about various services that we provide.

5. Submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) via SkillSelect

After meeting the requirements, the next step is applying for an Expression of Interest (EOI) through SkillSelect — the portal used by the Australian Government to whittle down PR candidates. An invitation will be extended to you if your profile aligns with the current demand in the labor market.

6. Gather Documents and Apply for PR Visa

Once the invitation is received, submit an online application for the applicable PR visa Australia. Generally required include:

  • Transcripts of records
  • Proof of English proficiency
  • Skills evaluation (by organizations such as ACS, Engineers Australia, etc.)
  • Medical and Criminal record checks

Advantages of Permanent Residency in Australia

Obtaining an Australian permanent resident status comes with plenty of advantages:

  • Unrestricted living and working in any region of Australia
  • Entitlement to Medicare (as part of public healthcare)
  • Ability to support select family members as they become permanent residents
  • Obtain Australian citizenship after a designated period
  • Unlimited international travel with Australia as the primary travel hub
  • Significantly improved access to higher education loans

Tips to Boost Your PR Chances

  • Study in Regional Areas of Australia: Provides extra points for permanent residency (PR) along with a greater probability for state nomination.
  • Boost Your English Score: Improved language skills translates to higher PR points.
  • Obtain Relevant Work Experience: Local work experience is highly regarded.
  • Apply for State Sponsorship: South Australia, Queensland, and Tasmania offer custom pathways toward permanent residency.

Also read our latest blog on Top 10 Part Time Jobs for University Students in Australia.

FAQs

1. How many PR points do you need at a minimum in Australia?

You must achieve at least 65 points to be eligible, but scoring higher will improve your chances of receiving an invitation significantly.

2. What are the international students’ best PR courses in Australia?

Some of the popular PR courses in Australia include nursing, engineering, IT, accountancy, and trade courses such as cookery and automotive studies.

3. After studies, how long does it take to get PR in Australia?

It varies depending on the visa subclass and your PR points. Generally, as long as you take the right steps and meet the criteria, it takes anywhere from 6 months to 2 years after graduation.

4. Can I apply for PR on a student visa?

Not directly, but you can prepare (e.g. take the English exam level, get skill assessed). After studies, you switch to the Temporary Graduate Visa (Subclass 485) and can then apply for PR.

5. Does studying in Australia guarantee PR?

Not really; there’s no guarantee that studying in Australia will lead to PR. You need to fulfill the requirements for PR in Australia including demand for occupation, points, and English language skills.

Final Thoughts

Understanding how to get PR (Permanent Residency) in Australia as an international student can provide life-altering possibilities. The process might require time and a detailed strategy, but having the right course along with the right experience, points, and the right policies makes PR achievable.

In any case, plan carefully, and if consideration of expert migration consultancy services is necessary, then do so — making your dream of obtaining a permanent resident status in Australia can become reality sooner than you anticipate.

title: Top 10 Part Time Jobs for University Students in Australia
excerpt: Explore the best part time jobs for university students in Australia, along with highest paying flexible jobs, remote positions, and visa-friendly roles.
html:
Top 10 Part Time Jobs for University Students in Australia

Are you looking for the best part time jobs to support yourself while studying in Australia? You are not alone. Flexible rewarding part time jobs in Australia are an integral part of the balance that thousands of university students across the country are trying to achieve.

We’ll look into the top 10 part time jobs for university students which include on-site work, and part time work from home opportunities. There is something here for everyone, whether you are an east coast local or an international student.

Why University Students Need Part Time Jobs

A part time job for students helps balance university life, cover living expenses, gain first hand experience, and enhance communication and time management skills. With Australia’s student-friendly job market, part time jobs for uni students are easily found in Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, and Perth.

Top 10 Part Time Jobs for University Students in Australia

1. Retail Assistant

The retail sector has one of the easiest entry options for people with little experience. Supermarkets, clothing stores, and electronic shops all provide retail jobs. Customer service is one of the primary retail practices, thus the retail job openings offer great customer service experience. The retail sector is known for flexible work scheduling, casual pay rates, and work.

  • Average Pay: $25–$30/hour
  • Shifts often available on weekends and evenings

2. Hospitality Staff (Waiter/Barista)

The café and restaurant sectors, along with supermarkets and bars, are always looking for vibrant and enthusiastic staff. If you enjoy fast-paced surroundings, we recommend these positions.

  • Average Pay: $23–$28/hour (plus tips)
  • Ideal for students with good communication skills

3. Tutoring (Online or In-person)

Fellow mates or school students are often looking for help with subject matter they are struggling with. If you excel in a particular subject, consider tutoring them.You can either do this face-to-face or as a part time work from home job.

  • Average Pay: $30–$60/hour
  • Flexible scheduling around your studies

4. Delivery Driver/Rider

Uber Eats, DoorDash, and Menulog are well-known food delivery contractors. These delivery services are popular among students, hence many students use bikes or cars to earn money in their free time.

  • Average Pay: $20–$25/hour + tips
  • Work when you want, perfect for night owls

5. Receptionist or Admin Assistant

Often Offices free up vacancies like receptionists and part-time admin work for students. It benefits students by allowing them to understand corporates.

  • Average Pay: $26–$32/hour
  • Great stepping stone into business careers

6. Freelancer (Design, Writing, Marketing)

Are you good with graphics, computer programming, video production, or creative writing? Students can complete projects for pay remotely using Upwork and Fiverr.

  • Average Pay: $25–$100/hour (depending on skill)
  • A top option for part time work from home jobs

7. Call Centre Agent

Phone support centers have evening and weekend shifts, great for students. A student needs to be very patient and possess good verbal communication skills.

  • Average Pay: $25–$30/hour
  • Experience in customer handling is a plus

8. Library or Campus Assistant

Occasionally, your university may have part-time job opportunities for their students. Things such as student library aides, laboratory aides, and event attendants sometimes fall under this category.

  • Average Pay: $25–$28/hour
  • Convenient location and flexible hours

9. Cleaner or Housekeeper

A lot of international students are employed in domestic, office, and hotel cleaning. The jobs generally require very little experience.

  • Average Pay: $22–$30/hour
  • Reliable income and consistent demand

10. Promotional Staff / Brand Ambassador

Help promote brands in events and at shopping malls or even the university. It is quite active work ideal for the people who love social settings.

  • Average Pay: $25–$35/hour
  • Short-term, high-paying gigs

You can also read our blog on Student Visa Working Hours in Australia 2025.

Where to Find Part Time Jobs in Australia

Students can find part-time jobs on these sites:

  • Seek Part Time Jobs
  • Indeed
  • Jora
  • Facebook Groups “Jobs for Students in Australia”
  • University career portals

Remember to customize your resume for every job application. Always mention your flexibility and any previous work experience.

Tips for Getting Hired

  • Craft a resume catered to students: Limit it to one page and emphasize soft skills.
  • Obtain a Tax File Number (TFN): Mandatory to legally work.
  • Submit applications as frequently as possible: Roles get filled quickly, particularly in hospitality and retail.
  • Be interview-ready: Know and rehearse your pitch so you are ready for the interview.

Also read our another blog on the Top 5 Things to Know Before Studying in Australia in 2025.

FAQs

1. What is the average pay for part time jobs in Australia?

The vast majority of part time jobs across Australia pay within the range of $23 to $30 per hour, particularly in hospitality, retail, and other industries where experience may influence wages. Retail and hospitality typically pay a bonus and weekend penalty rates.

2. How many hours can university students work on a student visa?

Student visa holders are permitted to work a maximum of 48 hours per fortnight during study sessions, while there are no limits on hours during vacation periods. Always verify visa compliance.

3. Can international students apply for part time jobs?

Of course! There are numerous part time student jobs for international students, particularly within the hospitality, retail, cleaning, and delivery industries.

4. What are the best part time work from home jobs for students?

In this case, part time jobs are freelancing, online tutoring, content writing, and virtual assistant as well as remote marketing roles specially designed for students.

5. Are there part time jobs available on campus?

Indeed so. Numerous Australian universities offer employment to uni students like research assistants, clerical aides, or event and service attendants working at the campus.

Conclusion

The right part time job can improve your life as a student living in Australia – allowing you to earn, socialize, and get some experience. Be it part time work from home jobs, weekend jobs, as well as regular ones located right at the campus, there is high availability to fetch the job of your dreams.

Similarly, remember to stay within the legal work limits of your visa and make the most out of the university experience!

title: Student Visa Working Hours in Australia 2025
excerpt: Learn about Student Visa Working Hours in Australia for 2025, along with holiday regulations, work hour limit, and tips for students to manage work and study.
html:
Student Visa Working Hours in Australia 2025

In case you are planning to study in Australia, it is important to pay attention to the Student Visa Working Hours policies, as your part time work options while studying are available up to 2025, Australia is still welcoming towards international students looking to work part-time while studying. However, the number of hours you are permitted to work is capped within set limits, which makes it important to always be updated if you want to ensure that you abide by the visa regulations.

This blog will cover everything regarding the Student Visa Working Hours, changes made to it, some exceptions, and help to strategize a work-study balance.

In Australia, the working hours for student visa limitations are implemented such that the work does not affect their studies as is the case from 2025. The Australia student visa working hours currently stands at:

  • During study periods: Up to 48 hours per fortnight (two weeks).
  • During scheduled holidays: Unlimited hours.

The 2023-2024 changes allowing Australian students to increased work opportunities while studying raised the previously allowed 40 hours per fortnight to 48 hours for better financial flexibility to students while still prioritizing their education.

Australia Student Visa Work Hour Limit: Key Details

The Australia student visa work hour limit was created so students can work to help financially support themselves without risking their grades. Students can now work as much as 48 hours within a two-week period, but it’s essential to understand how the allotted hours are tracked and how it affects your visa.

Note these certain guidelines:

  • Fortnightly Tracking: Work hours are calculated over a period of 14 days, as opposed to every week. For instance, you can work 30 hours one week, followed by 18 the following week.
  • Start of Permission: The students are entitled to begin working only after the course has officially commenced.
  • Unpaid Work Counts: Unpaid internships and volunteer work count towards the hours permitted on your student visa unless the placement is an officially recognized part of the course.
  • Multiple Jobs: Students may have several employers but the total combined hours should not surpass 48 hours worked in a fortnight.
  • Compliance is Crucial: Consistently working beyond the set limit for international students risks non-compliance which could result in a breach of visa conditions and possible future visa denials.

These details may seem technical in nature but they are essential in ensuring you accomplish your work goals compliantly without breaching your visa obligations.

Working Hours for Student Visa Holders During Holidays

Having access to student visas, especially for international students, and their associated student visa working hours during holidays is a major perk. The unique feature of student breaks as compared to other holidays is that there is absolutely no limit to the number of hours students can work. This is the ideal time to save money and gain plentiful experience as full-time interns or employees.

Bear in mind that “holidays” must be from the education provider. Taking personal leave will not provide you with the unlimited work cap.

International Student Working Hours: Special Cases

There are different situations in which international student work hours could vary:

  • Masters by Research and PhD students have unlimited working hours as soon as their courses begin.
  • If your course has compulsory work integrated learning placements, those hours do not contribute to your capped hours.

These exceptions make pursuing higher education a bit more accommodating for participants engaged in research intensive programs.

Why Australia Is a Top Choice for International Students

Flexible student visa working hours Australia offers, along with the rich educational opportunities and cultural diversity,makes it a highly favored country for international students. Part-time jobs offer various financial benefits and equip students with essential experience in the international marketplace.

Here is a sample of some of the most sought-after hospitality positions available to international students:

  • Hospitality (cafes, restaurants)
  • Retail (supermarkets, boutiques)
  • Administrative and clerical jobs
  • Tutoring and academic support roles
  • Freelance jobs, mostly in IT, graphic design, and marketing

With proper knowledge of a student visa’s working hours, students are able to pursue a career while studying in Australia. You can also read our blog on top 5 things you need to know before starting your study journey in Australia.

Tips to Manage Your Work and Study Balance

Harmonizing work life and educational activities poses a special challenge for international students, specifically because of the strict regulations on student visa working hours.

Below are some helpful tips for you:

Concentrate On Studies First

Always keep this in mind: the reason for being in Australia is for studying. Pay attention to issues related to your course and try to schedule work around classes and not the other way round. Keeping good academic progress is essential to keeping your visa.

Work Your Weeks Out In Advance

Organize your shifts in advance since the limit is 48 hours per fortnight. Make sure that you have a planner or an app where you can put down and track your work hours so that you do not breach your student visa hours of work.

Fully Utilize The Breaks Offered

Recognized academic breaks do give students the ability to work unlimited hours. Take these opportunities where you can get extra shifts, full time work, or even internships without having to worry about the visa restrictions on hours.

Choose Flexible Jobs

When searching for jobs, do so with the focus on part time work with flexible rosters. Sectors such as retail, hospitality, and freelancing usually have classes and examinations periods shifts which can easily be amended to suit student’s schedules.

Knowing Your Rights as an Employee

Make sure you know the Australian workplace regulations. You have the right to reasonable remuneration and a safe environment regardless of your visa conditions. If you’re confused, there is some free guidance available from the Fair Work Ombudsman, especially concerning international student work hour matters.

Don’t Overcommit

In this case, overcommitting means accepting too many work hours which can compromise your studies and harm your health. Strive to achieve a healthy balance geared towards earning money and experience while maintaining good academic grades.

Conclusion

Grasping the policies on foreign students’ work rights and student visa working hours Australia is extremely important to the overall experience as an international student. Limit work hours to the student visa hours of work, manage your time efficiently, and enjoy your study-work experience in Australia.

For those looking to study in Australia come 2025, knowledge of international student work hours and shifts in visa regulations will ensure greater success in studies and career.

How to Switch Courses or Colleges in Australia Without Risking Your Student Visa

Switching courses or colleges is a common decision for many international students in Australia. Whether you’re studying in Melbourne, Sydney, Brisbane, Adelaide, Perth, or Hobart, you’re not alone if you feel your current course, isn’t the right fit. Career goals can evolve, interests can shift, and personal circumstances change. However, it’s important to approach this transition carefully to avoid breaching your student visa (subclass 500) conditions. Here’s everything you need to know about changing your study path in Australia without risking your visa.

1. Understand Your Student Visa Conditions:  

As a student visa holder in Australia, you must:

  • Stay enrolled in a CRICOS-registered course
  • Maintain satisfactory course attendance and progress
  • Notify your education provider of any changes
  • Inform the Department of Home Affairs if required

Changing your course or institution may trigger visa implications, especially if you haven’t completed six months of your principal course.

2. The Six-Month Rule Explained:

 If you’re enrolled in a package of courses, your principal course is the highest qualification (usually a bachelor’s or master’s degree). You must complete at least six months of your principal course before transferring to another education provider in Australia.

Students in Sydney and Melbourne, for example, often want to switch early due to personal preferences or course mismatches. Transferring earlier requires a release letter.

3. Consult a Registered Migration Agent or Education Consultant:

Before making any changes, consult with a migration agent or international student advisor. Whether you’re studying in Brisbane, Perth, or Darwin, professional advice helps assess your visa status, enrolment conditions, and ensures your new course aligns with your career and PR goals in Australia.

4. Choose a CRICOS-Registered Education Provider:

Always transfer to a CRICOS-registered institution to remain compliant with your student visa. Ensure the new course is at the same or higher AQF level unless advised otherwise by your education or migration consultant.

Students in Adelaide and Hobart should also verify that their new institution offers full support for international student needs.

5. Obtain a New Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE):

Once you decide to transfer:

  • Get a new CoE (Confirmation of Enrolment) from your new provider
  • Cancel your current enrolment following proper procedures
  • Keep all documentation (letters, emails, CoEs) for future reference

Your visa remains valid as long as you are enrolled in a CRICOS course and follow the correct process.

6. Notify Immigration if Necessary:

In certain cases, you may need to inform the Department of Home Affairs, especially if:

  • There’s a gap between courses
  • Your course level changes (e.g., from a Bachelor’s to a Diploma)
  • You’re unsure about the impact on your visa conditions

This applies whether you’re transferring in Melbourne, Sydney, or any other state.

7. Let Professionals Guide You Through the Process

Switching courses or institutions in Australia can be overwhelming, especially for international students. That’s where Goodluck Education and Migration can help. We support students nationwide—from Perth to Brisbane, Adelaide to Hobart—and provide:

  • Expert advice from qualified migration agents
  • Course matching based on PR and career goals
  • Support in obtaining new CoEs and managing transitions
  • Full student visa compliance assistance

Conclusion You can change your course or college in Australia without risking your visa—but only if you follow the correct procedures. Always get professional advice, stay updated on your visa conditions, and keep detailed records of your transition.
